ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In a vacuum, a point charge with a charge of $q_{1} = +2.0 \times 10^{-6}   \mathrm{C}$ is fixed at point A, and a point charge with a charge of $q_{2} = +2.0 \times 10^{-6}   \mathrm{C}$ is placed at point B. The distance between A and B is $L = 2.0   \mathrm{m}$, and the electrostatic force constant is $k = 9.0 \times 10^{9}   \mathrm{N \cdot m^2 / C^2}$.

1. Determine the magnitude and direction of the Coulomb force experienced by the point charge at location B.
2. Find the magnitude of the electric field strength produced by a point charge at point A at point B.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
$9.0\times10^{-3}\mathrm{N}$, direction along the line AB to the right
$4.5\times10^{3}\mathrm{N/C}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a horizontal straight line, point A marked on the left side, point B marked on the right side, and A and B are on the same straight line. Reasoning calculation: The problem gives q1=+2.0×10^-6 C fixed at A, q2=+2.0×10^-6 C at B, the distance between A and B is L=2.0 m, k=9.0×10^9 N·m^2/C^2. The magnitude of the Coulomb force on the charge at B due to the charge at A is F=k|q1 q2|/L^2=(9.0×10^9)(2.0×10^-6)(2.0×10^-6)/(2.0)^2=9.0×10^-3 N. Since both charges are positive charges, they repel each other; in the figure A is on the left side of B, so the force on B is along the straight line AB to the right. The magnitude of the electric field intensity produced at point B by the point charge at A is E=k|q1|/L^2=(9.0×10^9)(2.0×10^-6)/(2.0)^2=4.5×10^3 N/C.
